items.title: Paquito D'Rivera — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: we play a piece written by Loria who was a type of obligatory music

ctx.x: In a way, the repertoire of this orchestra was similar to the way that you learned music, in terms of playing just a broad variety of different things, as opposed to focusing on one thing.

The only difference is that this orchestra was very commercially oriented. The music that we play by Mancini was [imitates rhythm] that big band type of sound was on old movies, I know that, was made famous by Ray Charles, it was a big hit in Havana in 1965 [imitates rhythm]. That was very commercial orientated, most of the time, but at the same time, we play a piece written by Loria who was a type of obligatory music, but mixed with pure percussion, I know that, and a drum solo, and even that contemporary atonal…
popular because it was very effective. Because it uses the two drummer they play in one combination, was a nice period; it was very different.
